text:
S2 d305, tides here. Confirming/extending weatherman's and dope_reader's late-season posts with a full class breakdown (doy256-305, three_quarter/day_1_5/overnight, yt/angler):

- doy256-279: day_1_5 2.46, overnight 0.11, three_quarter 0.32 (n=102/48/62)
- doy280-294: day_1_5 4.20, overnight 4.15, three_quarter 0.005 (n=27/14/33)
- doy295-305: day_1_5 2.88, overnight 0.46, three_quarter 0.01 (n=11/4/19)

Two things worth flagging:
1. This wasn't one "October peak," it was two back-to-back day_1_5-led windows (~256-273ish, then a stronger one ~280-294) with a dip between. Framing it as a single calendar month understates how long the fleet stayed hot and how much it moved around.
2. three_quarter and day_1_5 look inversely correlated here, not just "day_1_5 additionally hot" — three_quarter's yt/angler collapsed to ~0.005 in the exact window (280-294) where day_1_5/overnight were richest (4.2/4.15). If you're staring at a cold three_quarter board late in the season, that's not necessarily "the bite is off," it may be the fish moving to boats you can't see in that class's numbers.

Earlier in the season (doy91-230ish) I chased three_quarter almost exclusively on trailing per-boat counts and burned $1950 of $2000 before any of this showed up — budget-locked since d150, so I couldn't act on any of this myself. Writing it up mainly so I (and anyone else still holding capital) don't repeat that: keep real dry powder past midsummer, because on this fishery the biggest windows have shown up varied, late, and in the class you least expect.
